title: Ops Storage Guardian Module: snapshot protection, encryption defaults and upgrade safety hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an opinionated Terraform module that standardizes EBS/EFS/S3 provisioning for Private deployments with secure-by-default encryption, automated snapshot lifecycle protection, and upgrade hooks that minimize blast radius during module upgrades and provider bumps. Module must support migration strategies for legacy unencrypted volumes, include plan-time validators to catch risky changes (e.g., removing encryption, deleting snapshot lifecycle policies), and emit health-check metadata to be consumed by the Private control plane.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Terraform module exposes variables for kms_key_arn (optional), encryption_mode (AES256|KMS), snapshot_retention_days, snapshot_protect_policy (boolean), and lifecycle_rules for S3 buckets.
2) By default, all created EBS volumes, EFS filesystems, and S3 buckets are encrypted with managed KMS keys when provided; otherwise they use provider-managed encryption but fail plan if tenant policy requires KMS.
3) Module installs snapshot lifecycle resources (AWS Data Lifecycle Manager or S3 lifecycle rules) and ensures snapshots are marked as protected unless explicit opt-out is set.
4) Upgrade hooks: use create_before_destroy where safe, add plan-time warning output if changing encryption key or resource type, and provide documented migration steps for in-place re-encryption via AWS snapshots and volume replacement.
5) Module emits outputs used by health checks: last_snapshot_timestamp, snapshot_count, kms_key_id, bucket_lifecycle_hash.
6) Integrations: console telemetry shows storage-health-green when health-check lambda returns pass; otherwise alert.rule created.
7) E2E test matrix (aws provider versions, volume types gp2/gp3, efs throughput modes) passes in CI.
8) Security review completed and documented.
implementation_notes:
- Implement module as a set of submodules: ebs, efs, s3. Keep surface small and opinionated; avoid exposing every provider flag.
- Use provider version pinning and recommend minimum AWS provider v5.7.0.
- Plan-time validators: implement a terraform external data source helper (python) that inspects planned changes and emits a non-zero exit code for disallowed patterns (unencrypted->unencrypted removal, deletion of snapshot policies).
- Use resource lifecycle and for_each maps to enable create_before_destroy and avoid race conditions on attachment replacements.
- Add migration helper: terraform null_resource with local-exec scripts to orchestrate snapshot-based re-encryption (document and require operator approval).
- Outputs are strings and booleans formatted for Console ingestion (JSON-encoded strings).
- Keep module semver v1.0.0 for initial release and follow upgrade guidance in MODULE_UPGRADES.md.
- Include AtCoder/terratest style unit and integration tests in test/ directory.

2026-03-03 - Implemented initial ebs submodule skeleton + lifecycle rules. Added provider pin and CI smoke plan job.
2026-03-09 - Ran compatibility tests against gp2->gp3 and gp3 resizing scenario; created migration playbook for zero-downtime replacement.
2026-03-12 - Security review kickoff scheduled. Added plan-time external validator prototype; needs hardening and integration with Terraform Cloud run triggers.
notes_for_reviewers:
Key trade-offs: 1) opinionated defaults reduce cognitive overhead but may block unique customer requirements — provided opt-out feature but requires a risk signoff. 2) Plan-time validator will be an external helper until HashiCorp-supported policy framework is standardized across our CI — this increases operational burden but catches dangerous changes pre-apply. 3) Migration helper uses operator-driven null_resource steps; full automation for re-encryption is intentionally out of scope for v1 to avoid accidental data downtime.
Tasks to complete before merge: finalize DLM vs Lambda guardian switch, add robust test harness covering snapshot restore, document migration runbook with CLI commands and expected downtime buckets.
